> **Session focus:** *Educating collaborators, reporting of science, and framing researchable questions*

## Learning Objectives

* Teach statistical ideas to collaborators without losing nuance or trust
* Strengthen transparent reporting practices and replication mindset
* Frame researchable questions that align design, estimand, and analysis
* Integrate communication strategies with practical collaboration challenges

## Description of Activities

On 16 April (Block 2), we explored how to teach collaborators to communicate with statisticians, principles for reporting science, approaches for framing researchable questions, and perspectives on the “statistical pleasures” of medical collaborations. Activities emphasized bidirectional education and transparent, purpose-driven study design.

## Reflection (Gibbs Reflective Cycle)

### 1. Description

We practiced teaching collaborators how to work with statisticians, refreshed core reporting principles, and learned to frame questions that connect purpose, design, and estimand. The thread was reciprocity—learn their world and make ours understandable.

### 2. Feelings

I felt encouraged that teaching is a learnable craft and relieved to have concrete ways to explain hard ideas. The reporting session sharpened my sense that small documentation choices affect replicability and trust.

### 3. Evaluation

The bidirectional model felt practical and respectful. Reporting guidance was actionable—checklists and examples clarified expectations. More time to practice turning vague questions into answerable ones would help.

### 4. Analysis

Listening precedes explaining; partnership beats one‑way service. Repeated, low‑stakes practice is how teaching skills stick. Starting with the right question matters—great analysis cannot fix a mis‑specified question. Clear reporting is how we show our work with integrity.

### 5. Conclusion

Teaching, framing questions, and reporting are mutually reinforcing. They move collaborations from transactions to co-creation, anchoring rigor in shared understanding and transparent documentation.

### 6. Action Plan

I will prepare analogies and visuals for common concepts, adopt a reproducibility/reporting checklist, and develop a short “question-framing” guide (purpose, estimand, outcomes, design, constraints). I’ll schedule pre-meet reads of clinical background to align language and goals.
